title: Protesters testing maximum tolerance limits during ASEAN, says PNP
summary: The statement follows the arrest of hundreds of activists over the ASEAN Summit weekend, including 200 anti-Pax Silica protesters in Muntinlupa.

blocks.text: Protesters clash with police officers during a demonstration that coincides with the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Leaders' Summit and Related Summits in Manila on Nov. 15, 2026.

MANILA, Philippines — The Philippine National Police (PNP) warned protesters Monday, November 16, not to "mistake maximum tolerance and restraint for weakness" as it defended police operations that led to hundreds of arrests during the opening weekend of the ASEAN summit.

PNP spokesperson Allen Rae Co denied that police had barred activists from approaching summit venues in Pasay City, saying officers had exercised restraint despite confrontations that left several police personnel injured.
Co also denied that police instigated a confrontation with protesters opposing the US-led Pax Silica initiative in Sucat, Muntinlupa City, where more than 200 people were arrested.
"We negotiated for 12 hours in Muntinlupa. We asked them to clear the road because no one could pass, but they insisted on going. Isn't marching part of protesting?" Co said.
He described the protesters' blockade as a "disruption" and questioned the groups' intentions.
Co argued that protest organizations forfeited their right to peaceful assembly when their objective was to "create maximum disturbance and inconvenience to others."
Progressive groups, however, estimated that more than 300 people had been arrested in connection with demonstrations during the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) summit.
Co also addressed reports of police harassment of journalists covering the demonstrations, saying the incidents were unintentional.

"We understand, of course, that you are journalists, and you are bound by duty to report what is happening to the public. But during these times, if your positioning or actions are unclear, and you act as if you're part of the protestors … our officers were injured," Co said.
Journalists covering the protests have reported harassment by police, raising concerns over their ability to document the demonstrations.
Human rights watchdog Amnesty International Philippines called for the immediate and unconditional release of the arrested protesters in a statement Sunday.
